About Mra Shamba Facts

A Kenyan farming brand for young people.

Who we are

Mra Shamba Facts is a farming brand that shares simple, practical tips on crops, tomato production, livestock and organic methods on YouTube, TikTok and Facebook.

Our goal is to reach as many people as possible and empower them through agriculture.

Crops

Start with crops that grow fast and have a ready market.

Tomatoes

  • Use certified seed and start in a nursery bed.
  • Stake plants to keep fruit off the soil.
  • Water at the base, not on the leaves.
  • Remove diseased leaves early.

Kale (sukuma wiki)

  • Give plants space for good airflow.
  • Pick the lower leaves so the plant keeps producing.
  • Add compost between harvests.
  • Transplant seedlings when they are sturdy.

Livestock

Simple care routines for healthier animals.

Care basics

Healthy animals start with clean housing, clean water and good feed.

Poultry

Keep the coop dry and ventilated, vaccinate on schedule, and always provide clean water.

Goats and sheep

Provide raised, dry housing, deworm regularly and give enough roughage.

Dairy

Milk in a clean place, keep a record for each cow, and call a vet early when something looks wrong.

Manure feeds the soil

Animal manure, once composted, returns nutrients to your crops. It links your livestock and your vegetable beds.

More farming facts

Farming Facts

Know-how for every stage of your farming journey.

Quick facts

Short, useful ideas you can apply this week.

Test your soil

A soil test shows what fertilizer you need, so you stop paying for what you don't.

Water at the right time

Morning or evening watering loses less water to the sun.

Keep records

Write down costs and sales for every crop. It shows what actually pays.

Use extension services

County agricultural officers give advice on pests, seed and training.

Organic soil care

  • Make compost from farm waste.
  • Rotate crops each season.
  • Mulch to hold moisture.

How to start farming

A simple path for a first-time farmer.

  1. Get land and water

    Even a small plot works. Check that you can reach water all year.

  2. Test the soil

    Know your soil before you buy seed or fertilizer.

  3. Pick one crop or animal

    Start with one that sells well in your area and learn it properly.

  4. Plan your costs

    List seed, labor, inputs and transport, then compare with expected sales.

  5. Plant, record, improve

    Keep notes each season and adjust what did not work.

Frequently asked questions

Is the farming advice free?

Yes. Our videos and posts on YouTube, TikTok and Facebook are free to watch.

Can I suggest a topic?

Yes. Leave a comment below or send us a message on the Contact page.

Should I follow your tips exactly?

Conditions differ by region, so check with your county agricultural officer before big decisions like fertilizer or vaccines.
